carousels.name: 4 CBT tools therapists use for p*rn addiction

slides.title: 4 tools therapists use to treat [[p*rn addiction.]]
slides.sub: You can start using them tonight.

slides.title: Thought [[tracking]]
slides.body: Write down the exact thought before a p*rn urge: "I'm bored." "I deserve it." Seeing the thought on paper makes it easier to question.

slides.title: Reframing
slides.body: Swap "I need p*rn to relax" for "I want to relax — what else works?" Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) teaches this one thought at a time.

slides.title: Exposure & [[response]] prevention
slides.body: Notice the trigger, feel the p*rn urge, and don't act on it — on purpose. Each time, the urge loses a little of its pull.

slides.title: A written [[coping plan]]
slides.body:
Decide in advance: "When a p*rn urge hits, I will ___."

A plan made calmly beats a decision made mid-craving.

carousels.name: Your p*rn use affects her self-esteem too

slides.title: Your p*rn addiction isn't only [[hurting you.]]
slides.sub: What partners say it does to how they see themselves.

slides.title: "Am I [[not enough?]]"
slides.body: Many partners say discovering p*rn use made them compare themselves to what's on the screen. That comparison hurts.

slides.title: Research [[agrees]]
slides.body: One university study of 308 women linked a partner's frequent p*rn use to lower relationship satisfaction — partly through lower self-esteem. It doesn't prove cause, but the pattern is real for many couples.

slides.title: It's [[not]] about them
slides.body: P*rn addiction is about the addiction, not your partner's worth. Say that out loud: "This is my struggle, not your fault."

slides.title: Rebuild her [[confidence]]
items: Be honest about your p*rn use, without excuses.
Show progress in quitting p*rn, don't just promise it.
Get support together if you need it.
slides.note: Partners: what helped you feel secure again? Share below 👇

slides.title: Sunday night anxiety is [[a p*rn relapse trap.]]
slides.sub: Why the night before Monday hits so hard.

slides.title: The Monday [[dread]]
slides.body: Work, deadlines, a whole week ahead — and anxiety builds all evening. For many people, p*rn becomes the way to escape that dread.

slides.title: The "[[fresh start]]" lie
slides.body: "I'll watch p*rn tonight and start clean on Monday." That thought has restarted more streaks than any other.

slides.title: Make Sunday [[lighter]]
slides.body: Plan the week on Sunday afternoon, not at midnight. A clear head on Sunday evening makes p*rn far less tempting.

slides.title: Your Sunday [[plan]]
items: Blocker on and no "last p*rn before Monday."

carousels.name: Why we need to talk about p*rn addiction

slides.title: We joke about p*rn. [[We never talk about p*rn addiction.]]
slides.sub: And that silence keeps so many people stuck.

slides.title: Jokes [[hide]] the problem
slides.body: Memes and jokes make p*rn seem harmless and universal. Meanwhile, people struggling with p*rn addiction feel like they can't say anything.

slides.title: Silence [[feeds]] shame
slides.body: When nobody talks about p*rn addiction, everyone thinks they're the only one. That isolation is exactly what keeps the loop going.

slides.title: Talking [[helps]]
slides.body: Support groups work largely because they remove that isolation. One honest conversation about p*rn can change someone's year.

slides.title: How to [[start]] the conversation
items: Share this post — it opens the door.
Don't laugh when someone mentions p*rn struggles.
Point people to real help, not shame.

carousels.name: What a good p*rn-free day looks like

slides.title: What a good [[p*rn-free day]] actually looks like.
Start [[offline]]
slides.body: No phone for 30 minutes. Sunlight, water, movement. A calm morning makes p*rn urges easier to handle later.

slides.title: Plan the [[danger hours]]
slides.body: Know when your p*rn urges usually hit — and put something there: gym, a call, a walk.

slides.title: Wind [[down]], not out
slides.body: Screens off by a set time. P*rn blocker on. Phone charging outside the bedroom. The night is where most p*rn relapses happen.

slides.title: Two-minute [[check-in]]
slides.body: Did I feel any p*rn urges today? What helped? What's tomorrow's plan? Small reflections add up to big change.
